title: Programmes for those not watching
titleChinese: 给不看屏幕的人设计的电视节目
paragraphs: OK, I'm not proud of it, but sometimes when I'm watching TV, I might not actually be watching. Sometimes I'm just more tempted by my phone. Be honest, do you do the same? If you do, then we're not alone, lots of us watch TV with our phones in our hands. How is TV changing to accommodate this?

Let's start by looking at the data. Studies have investigated different countries across the world and many of them reported that most people use their phone while watching TV. While the classic stereotype is that it's younger people who find it hard to put their phone down, the data actually shows that second-screening is common in most age groups under 55. Younger age groups are more likely to be looking at social media or food delivery apps, while older age groups prefer banking, e-commerce and travel.

How are producers dealing with this? A number of screenwriters have reported being told that they need to make programmes easier to follow for distracted viewers. Reports say that showrunners have asked for more exposition in dialogue, repetition of plot points and increased use of voice-over to make things clearer for those who aren't looking. Some critics and viewers have complained that this could be making series less complex and dialogue less natural.

Second screens are not the only reason that these things happen. Television drama writing developed from radio drama writing, which has to use dialogue to compensate for the lack of visuals. When books are adapted for TV or film, one challenge is how to tell the whole story with less narration. All this means that exposition has often been a feature of TV writing. As series became more prestigious and cinematic since the early 2000s, this clear signposting of plot points had become less common.

Of course, TV viewers and TV programmes are not all the same. There is space for both casual and more complex programmes. Maybe the most important thing is for us to remember when to put our phones down.
chineseParagraphs: 好吧，我对此并不自豪，但有时我看电视的时候，可能并没有真正在看。有时候手机对我更有吸引力。说实话，你也这样吗？如果你也这样，那我们并不孤单，我们很多人都是手里拿着手机看电视。电视节目为了适应这一现象正在发生怎样的变化呢？
让我们先看看数据。研究调查了全球不同国家，其中许多研究报告称，大多数人在看电视时会使用手机。虽然传统的刻板印象是年轻人很难放下手机，但数据显示，“第二屏幕”现象在55岁以下的大多数年龄段中都很常见。年轻群体更可能在看社交媒体或外卖软件，而年长群体则更喜欢使用银行、电商和旅游类应用。
制片人如何应对这种情况呢？许多编剧透露，他们被告知需要让节目更容易被分心的观众理解。有报道称，节目制作人要求在对话中加入更多解释性内容、重复情节要点，并增加画外音的使用，以便让那些不看屏幕的人也能明白。一些评论家和观众抱怨说，这可能会降低剧集的复杂性，并使对话显得不那么自然。
第二屏幕并不是这些现象发生的唯一原因。电视剧剧本创作源于广播剧剧本创作，广播剧必须依靠对话来弥补视觉画面的缺失。当书籍被改编成电视剧或电影时，挑战之一是如何用更少的旁白讲述完整的故事。所有这些都意味着，解释性内容一直是电视剧写作的一个特点。自21世纪初以来，随着剧集变得更加精品化和电影化，这种清晰标注情节转折点的做法变得不那么常见了。
当然，电视观众和电视节目并非都一样。既存在轻松休闲的节目，也有更复杂的节目。也许最重要的是，我们要记住什么时候该放下手机。

vocabulary.entry: tempt /tempt/ v. 诱惑，吸引
vocabulary.example: The offer of a free trip tempted him into booking.
vocabulary.translation: 免费旅行的提议吸引他预订了。

vocabulary.entry: accommodate /əˈkɒmədeɪt/ v. 适应，容纳（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店最多可容纳500位客人。

vocabulary.entry: stereotype /ˈsteriətaɪp/ n. 刻板印象，模式化观念
vocabulary.example: There are many stereotypes about people from different cultures.
vocabulary.translation: 关于不同文化背景的人存在许多刻板印象。

vocabulary.definition: 第二屏幕（观看电视时使用其他设备的行为）（口语，专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: second-screening /ˌsekənd ˈskriːnɪŋ/ n. 第二屏幕（观看电视时使用其他设备的行为）（口语，专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Second-screening has become a common habit for many TV viewers.
vocabulary.translation: 第二屏幕已经成为许多电视观众的常见习惯。

vocabulary.entry: e-commerce /ˈiː kɒmɜːs/ n. 电子商务（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: E-commerce has changed the way people shop.
vocabulary.translation: 电子商务改变了人们的购物方式。

vocabulary.entry: screenwriter /ˈskriːnraɪtə(r)/ n. 编剧（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The screenwriter won an award for the film's script.
vocabulary.translation: 这位编剧因电影剧本获奖。

vocabulary.entry: distracted /dɪˈstræktɪd/ adj. 分心的，注意力分散的
vocabulary.example: He seemed distracted during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 他在会议期间似乎心不在焉。

vocabulary.definition: 节目统筹（电视行业术语）
vocabulary.entry: showrunner /ˈʃəʊrʌnə(r)/ n. 节目统筹（电视行业术语）
vocabulary.example: The showrunner is responsible for the creative direction of the series.
vocabulary.translation: 节目统筹负责剧集的创意方向。

vocabulary.definition: 解释性内容（文学/戏剧术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: exposition /ˌekspəˈzɪʃn/ n. 解释性内容（文学/戏剧术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The play opens with a lot of exposition.
vocabulary.translation: 这部剧以大量解释性内容开场。

vocabulary.entry: dialogue /ˈdaɪəlɒɡ/ n. 对话，对白
vocabulary.example: The movie has some very funny dialogue.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有一些非常有趣的对话。

vocabulary.entry: repetition /ˌrepəˈtɪʃn/ n. 重复（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Repetition is a useful learning tool.
vocabulary.translation: 重复是一种有用的学习工具。

vocabulary.definition: 情节转折点（文学/戏剧术语）
vocabulary.entry: plot point /ˈplɒt pɔɪnt/ n. 情节转折点（文学/戏剧术语）
vocabulary.example: The plot point at the end of the first act surprised everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 第一幕结尾的情节转折让所有人都感到惊讶。

vocabulary.entry: voice-over /ˈvɔɪs əʊvə(r)/ n. 画外音（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The documentary used a voice-over to explain the images.
vocabulary.translation: 这部纪录片使用画外音来解释画面。

vocabulary.entry: critic /ˈkrɪtɪk/ n. 评论家，批评者
vocabulary.example: Critics of the plan say it's too expensive.
vocabulary.translation: 该计划的批评者说它太昂贵了。

vocabulary.entry: compensate /ˈkɒmpenseɪt/ v. 补偿，弥补（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Nothing can compensate for the loss of a loved one.
vocabulary.translation: 失去亲人是什么也弥补不了的。

vocabulary.definition: 视觉画面，视觉效果（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: visual /ˈvɪʒuəl/ n. 视觉画面，视觉效果（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film has stunning visuals.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有令人惊叹的视觉效果。

vocabulary.entry: adapt /əˈdæpt/ v. 改编，适应
vocabulary.example: The novel was adapted for television.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说被改编成了电视剧。

vocabulary.entry: narration /nəˈreɪʃn/ n. 叙述，旁白（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The narration adds depth to the story.
vocabulary.translation: 旁白为故事增添了深度。

vocabulary.definition: 有声望的，受尊敬的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: prestigious /preˈstɪdʒəs/ adj. 有声望的，受尊敬的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She graduated from a prestigious university.
vocabulary.translation: 她毕业于一所名牌大学。

vocabulary.definition: 电影的，电影制作的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: cinematic /ˌsɪnəˈmætɪk/ adj. 电影的，电影制作的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film has a very cinematic quality.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影具有很强的电影质感。

vocabulary.entry: signposting /ˈsaɪnpəʊstɪŋ/ n. 清晰标注，指引（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Clear signposting of plot points helps viewers follow the story.
vocabulary.translation: 对情节转折点的清晰标注有助于观众跟上故事。

vocabulary.entry: casual /ˈkæʒuəl/ adj. 随意的，非正式的
vocabulary.example: He wore casual clothes to the party.
vocabulary.translation: 他穿着休闲装参加派对。

vocabulary.entry: put down /ˌpʊt ˈdaʊn/ phr. v. 放下（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Please put down your phones and listen to the teacher.
vocabulary.translation: 请放下手机，听老师讲课。
